referenced_urls.title: PROBE: Frontier Coding Agents Find Different Bugs Than Maintainers Fix

relevance: Highlights mismatch between agent bug-finding and maintainer priorities.

media.description: Abstract excerpt of PROBE, a benchmark of 2,457 bugs fixed over 18 months in 20 GitHub repos; coding agents reach under 21% recall and under 9% precision at repository-wide bug discovery.
media.ocr_text: Proactive bug discovery is an important software-engineering problem. Even though coding agents are already widely deployed in this domain, their capabilities remain understudied. In particular, the challenging task of finding all bugs that human maintainers would repair across an entire repository has not been studied yet. To close this gap, we introduce PROBE, a benchmark consisting of all 2,457 bugs fixed over the course of 18 months across 20 diverse GitHub repositories, together with a method for matching candidate findings to this partial reference set. We evaluate coding agents across frontier models and find they all achieve a recall of below 21% and a precision of less than 9% with respect to the reference set.
